comment: What each classic port understands, per game family: the line types, sector types, flag bits and thing numbers a map may use and still load. Numbers are facts read from the ports' own code (Chocolate Doom 2026-10-13 for vanilla Doom, Heretic, Hexen and Strife: P_CrossSpecialLine, P_UseSpecialLine, P_ShootSpecialLine, P_SpawnSpecials, P_PlayerInSpecialSector, info.c doomednum; dsda-doom for Boom and MBF; the MBF21 specification for MBF21). Ranges are written 'a-b', lists comma-separated. 'sectorBits' are Boom's generalized sector bits a port honours over the base type; 'generalized' says whether Boom's generalized line types (0x2F80-0x7FFF) load. 'limits' is 'vanilla' (the 1993 engine's static limits) or 'format' (only what the file format can hold). 'complevel' is what dsda-doom, Woof and Nugget are told; 'umapinfo' whether the export writes a UMAPINFO lump for the map's name, music, sky and next map.
